- Key constraints you mentioned: strict egress rules, DNS resolution via internal resolver, mTLS required for service-to-service, and central procurement timeline.

Technical asks we agreed to follow up on
1) VPC endpoints model (interface endpoints vs. VPC peering) and recommended approach for AWS.
2) IP allowlist for firewall — exact CIDR ranges from our egress to include.
3) DNS egress behavior — whether you need split-horizon DNS or we should support forwarding to your resolver.
4) mTLS handshake details and client cert provisioning flow.

Attachments I will share: VPC connectivity diagram, connector IP list, and an mTLS checklist. Jonas will follow up with a short config example for the SDK auth + mTLS.

Next steps
- Jonas: example mTLS config + TLS cert rotation notes (by EOD Thu PT).
- FinPay network team (Bob): confirm whether interface endpoints are acceptable or if peering is required, and share expected blackout windows for any routing changes.
- Marissa: will send a preliminary statement of work and pricing for Dedicated/Private options.

If anything above is off, tell me and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll schedule a 30-minute technical sync for next week with your network team.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren — that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- For security reasons we prefer AWS interface VPC endpoints (PrivateLink) rather than VPC peering. Peering is allowed only for infra teams and requires extra approvals.
- Our firewall team needs a stable list of outbound IP ranges for your connectors. Ideally we get a /24 granularity per region.
- For DNS, we run an internal resolver that must handle redwood.* names — we can do conditional forwarding to your resolver if you provide an IP for forwarders.
- On mTLS: we can accept client certs from Redwood if you support cert rotation and CRL/OCSP. Also please confirm whether mutual auth will be at TLS layer or application-level with JWTs.

We can set up a technical sync with our network engineer Bob Torres — he’s cc’d. He’s available next Tue/Wed morning PST.

One request: can you share a brief checklist of what we need to change on our side (security groups, route tables, DNS entries)? That will help speed approvals.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@finpay.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: VPC endpoints + allowlist — mTLS & SDK config example

Hi Alice — quick technical note and example to make the mTLS path concrete. TL;DR: we support TLS mutual auth at the transport layer (mTLS) and optionally application-layer JWTs for routing/claims. Cert rotation is handled by our SDK via a short-lived client cert retrieved from the customer keyserver (or we can integrate with your Vault/HSM).

Example (high level)
- TLS: Redwood connector expects client cert + key (PEM) on the TLS handshake. We validate against a CA you trust or use our CA; both models supported.
- SDK: you can bootstrap with either (A) long-lived client certs that you rotate, or (B) our rotation API that pulls short-lived certs from your key management endpoint via a signed request.

Sample curl (mTLS)
curl --cert client.pem --key client.key https://connect.redwood.internal/v1/predict -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

SDK snippet (pseudo-Python)
from redwood_sdk import Connector
conn = Connector(endpoint="https://connect.redwood.internal", client_cert_path="/etc/ssl/client.pem", client_key_path="/etc/ssl/client.key")
resp = conn.predict(model="rwd-embed-1", input="...", structured_output=True)

Notes:
- If you prefer OCSP stapling / CRL checks, we can run that as part of our TLS termination for Private deployments.
- For DNS: we will accept a conditional forwarder to our resolver (we’ll provide IPs once the VPC endpoints are provisioned).
- IP list: see attached CSV with current connector egress CIDRs per region. We can reserve a /24 if needed; talk with Marissa for pricing impact.

Happy to run through these lines in the technical sync — I’ll be on the call next Tue.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
